key: IN-1629
title: "booking page: show when each class ends"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:client]
sources: [IN-1629, IN-3740]
---

## Intent
The booking page shows only the start time of each slot. Show its end time next to it (a Slot has a start and an end, specs/product.md), in the viewer's zone (PRD-2).

## Acceptance
- Given a slot from 10:00 to 11:00, when the booking page shows it, then it reads 10:00–11:00.
- Given a viewer in another zone, when the booking page shows the slot, then start and end are both in the viewer's zone.
- Given the booking page, when the end time is added, then the start time it shows now is not removed or changed.

## Boundaries
- Must not change how slots are stored.

Allowed by AUT-1 (new columns, filters or fields that add to what is there and take nothing away).

Request (mail): "Our booking page shows only the start time of each class. Could it show when the class ends as well?"
Request IN-3740 (desk): "the slot list on the booking page only shows when a slot starts. Customer wants the end time too."

key: IN-1699
title: "CSV export: a comma in a client name shifts the columns"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:analytics]
sources: [IN-1699]
---

## Intent
The CSV export breaks when a client name has a comma in it: the columns shift by one from there. Quote fields that hold a comma, a quote or a line break (RFC 4180), so every row keeps its columns.

## Acceptance
- Given a client named "Smith, Jones & Co", when the export is generated, then the row has the same number of columns as the header and the name reads back whole.
- Given a name with a double quote, when the export is generated, then the quote is doubled inside a quoted field and reads back whole.
- Given a row with no comma, quote or line break, when the export is generated, then it is not changed.

## Boundaries
- Must not add, remove, rename or reorder columns (PRD-3).
- Must not change the date or time format.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes and small features inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

Request (chat): "the CSV export breaks when a client name has a comma in it. the columns shift by one from there."

key: IN-2180
title: "bookings list: column with a person's no-show count"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-2180]
---

## Intent
Add a column to the team's bookings list that shows how many times the person on each booking did not turn up, counted from bookings already marked as no-shows.

## Acceptance
- Given a person with 2 bookings marked no-show and 5 attended, when the bookings list shows one of their bookings, then the no-show column reads 2.
- Given a person with no no-shows, when the list shows their booking, then the column reads 0.
- Given the bookings list, when the column is added, then no existing column is removed or reordered, and the public booking page does not show the count.

## Boundaries
- Must not change or rewrite stored bookings or attendance marks.
- Must not show the count outside the team's bookings list.

Allowed by AUT-1 (new columns, filters or fields that add to what is there and take nothing away).

Request (desk): "a studio asks for a column on the bookings list that shows how often a person did not turn up."

key: IN-4082
title: "week view: hover shows who booked"
status: open

## Intent
Hovering over a booking in week view shows its time but not who booked it. Add the name of the person who booked to that hover card.

## Acceptance
- Given a booking by Ana Silva at 10:00, when a team member hovers it in week view, then the card shows 10:00 and Ana Silva.
- Given the hover card, when the name is added, then the time it showed is still there.
- Given the public booking page, when anyone views it, then no booker's name is shown there: names are not public.

## Boundaries
- Must not show bookers' names outside the team's week view.

Allowed by AUT-1 (new columns, filters or fields that add to what is there and take nothing away).

Request (desk): "Ticket: hovering over a booking in week view shows its time but not who booked it."

title: "booking page: confirm button to say 'OK'"
status: closed
reason: contradicts-spec
labels: [from:product]
sources: [IN-4295]
---

Closed: DES-5 says buttons say what they do, a verb and its object ("Cancel booking", not "OK"). A button that says 'OK' breaks that rule. To change it, change DES-5 first.

Request (chat): "make the confirm button on the booking page just say 'OK'. shorter is cleaner. i want it this week."

key: IN-5260-calendar
title: "confirmation email: 'Add to calendar' opens a blank page"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-5260]
---

## Intent
The 'Add to calendar' link in the booking confirmation email opens a blank page. Make it hand the booking to the person's calendar as an event with the booking's start and end. Split from ticket IN-5260, which merged two problems; the logo is IN-5260.

## Acceptance
- Given a booking confirmation email, when 'Add to calendar' is opened, then the person gets a calendar event with the booking's start, end and zone (ADR-0001).
- Given the same link opened twice, when the event is added again, then it carries the same stable id (ADR-0002), so the calendar does not show two events.
- Given the link, when it is opened by someone without an account, then it does not ask for a login.

## Boundaries
- Must not read anything back from the person's calendar (ADR-0002).

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes and small features inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

Request (desk, merged by tove · 2 reports): "the client's logo is stretched in the booking confirmation email, and the 'Add to calendar' link in the same email opens a blank page."

key: IN-5260
title: "confirmation email: the client's logo is stretched"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-5260]
---

## Intent
The client's logo is stretched in the booking confirmation email. Show it at its own aspect ratio. Ticket IN-5260 merged two problems; the 'Add to calendar' link is its own issue, IN-5260-calendar.

## Acceptance
- Given a client logo of 400×100 px, when the confirmation email renders, then the logo keeps its 4:1 ratio.
- Given a square logo, when the confirmation email renders, then it is not stretched or cropped.
- Given the email's other content, when the fix ships, then it does not change.

## Boundaries
- Must not change the client's uploaded logo file.
- Must not change the sender address (see IN-8087).

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes and small features inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

Request (desk, merged by tove · 2 reports): "the client's logo is stretched in the booking confirmation email, and the 'Add to calendar' link in the same email opens a blank page."

key: IN-6901
title: "booking page: date picker cannot be used with the keyboard"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-6901]
---

## Intent
The date picker on the booking page cannot be used with the keyboard alone. Make every part of it reachable and usable by keyboard.

## Acceptance
- Given the booking page, when a person tabs to the date picker, then focus lands on it and is visible.
- Given focus in the picker, when the arrow keys are pressed, then focus moves by day and week, and Enter picks the date.
- Given focus in the picker, when Escape is pressed, then it closes without changing the date and focus does not leave the page.

## Boundaries
- Must not change how dates are parsed or stored (SCHED-4471, PRD-2).
- Must not change the picker's look for mouse users.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes and small features inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

Request (desk): "the date picker on the booking page cannot be used with the keyboard alone."

key: IN-7404
title: "booking page: icon buttons need accessible labels"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-7404]
---

## Intent
A screen reader reads every icon button on the booking page as just 'button'. Give each one an accessible label that says what it does, a verb and its object (DES-5).

## Acceptance
- Given a screen reader on the booking page, when it reaches the next-week icon button, then it reads a label such as "Show next week".
- Given every icon button on the booking page, when the page is audited, then each has a non-empty accessible name.
- Given the page, when the labels are added, then nothing visible changes, and a label does not read just "OK" or "button".

## Boundaries
- Must not change the buttons' look or what they do.

Allowed by AUT-1 (copy changes in the product's own interface).

Request (desk): "a screen reader user says every icon button on the booking page is read out as just 'button'. Give them proper labels."

key: IN-7516
title: "settings page: fix typo 'Calender' → 'Calendar'"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:product]
sources: [IN-7516]

## Intent
The settings page says 'Calender'. Change it to 'Calendar'.

## Acceptance

- Given the product's interface copy, when it is searched, then 'Calender' is not found anywhere.

## Boundaries
- Must not rename settings keys, ids or URLs; copy only.

Allowed by AUT-1 (copy changes in the product's own interface).

Request (chat): "typo on the settings page: 'Calender'. should be 'Calendar'."

key: IN-8087
title: "reminder emails: send from no-reply@ instead of bookings@?"
status: open
labels: [needs-human, from:product, from:client]
sources: [IN-8087, IN-8530]
---

## Question
Product asks to send reminder emails from no-reply@ instead of bookings@, because replies pile up (IN-8087). A client told all their patients to allow mail from bookings@ so reminders stay out of spam, and asks us not to change it (IN-8530). Should the sender address change?

## Options
1. Send reminders from no-reply@ for every account.
2. Keep bookings@ as the sender; handle the replies instead (auto-reply, or route them to the account's own inbox).
3. Add a per-account sender setting, with bookings@ as the default.

## Recommendation
Option 2.

## Why
Because a client told us they rely on bookings@ (IN-8530), so a change to it needs a person (AUT-2); the problem in IN-8087 is the replies, which option 2 solves without changing the address.

Requests: IN-8087 (chat) "send reminder emails from no-reply@ instead of bookings@. the replies just pile up." · IN-8530 (mail) "We told all our patients to allow mail from bookings@ so reminders don't land in spam. Please don't change that address."

key: IN-8541
title: "CSV export: dd/mm dates for EU accounts, or keep mm/dd?"
status: open
labels: [needs-human, from:support, from:client]
sources: [IN-8541, IN-9776]
---

## Question
Support asks to write the dates in the CSV export as dd/mm, not mm/dd, for EU accounts (IN-8541). A client's payroll import reads those dates as mm/dd today and asks us not to flip them (IN-9776). Should the export change its existing date format?

## Options
1. Change the existing date columns to dd/mm for EU accounts.
2. Keep the existing columns as they are; add a new date column in the account's locale format.
3. Keep the export as it is; SCHED-4446 adds the UTC offset, and EU clients' tools format the date.

## Recommendation
Option 2.

## Why
Because a client told us their payroll relies on mm/dd (IN-9776), so changing it needs a person (AUT-2); SCHED-4446 keeps the start and end columns as they are, and PRD-3 says an export never loses a column it had.

Requests: IN-8541 (desk) "EU accounts want the dates in the CSV export as dd/mm, not mm/dd. Should be a one-line change." · IN-9776 (mail, ilse · studio · auckland) "Our payroll import reads the dates in your CSV export as month first, mm/dd, the way they come today. Please do not flip them to day first under us."

status: open

## Intent
The 'today' button is missing from week view on phones. Show it there, as on larger screens.

## Acceptance
- Given week view on a 375 px wide screen, when it renders, then the 'today' button is visible.
- Given that button, when it is tapped, then week view jumps to the current week in the viewer's zone.
- Given week view on a desktop screen, when it renders, then the 'today' button does not move or change.

## Boundaries

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes and small features inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

Request (desk): "Ticket: the 'today' button is missing from week view on phones."

key: IN-9276
title: "week view: compact layout that fits a whole day on one screen"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:client]
sources: [IN-9276]
blocked-by: [SCHED-4468]
---

## Intent
A front desk needs a compact week view that fits a whole day on one screen. Build it as a denser layout from the spacing scale (DES-3), as an option next to the current view. It waits for SCHED-4468: until margins are on the spacing scale, a denser layout cannot come from it.

## Acceptance
- Given a team member who turns on the compact view, when week view renders on a 1080 px tall screen, then 08:00 to 20:00 fits without scrolling.
- Given the compact view, when its CSS is read, then every spacing value is a spacing-scale token, and no font size is below the type scale (DES-1).
- Given a team member who does not turn it on, when week view renders, then it does not change.

## Boundaries
- Must not replace the current week view.
- Must not add spacing values outside the 4 px scale.

Allowed by AUT-1 (a denser layout built on the spacing scale (DES-3)).

Request (mail): "URGENT: our front desk needs a compact week view that fits a whole day on one screen, before Friday."

key: SCHED-4412
title: "colours: move hard-coded colours to design tokens"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:product]
---

## Intent
Components still carry raw hex values. Move every colour in components to the `--color-*` tokens (DES-2). Nothing visible changes. Until this ships, a new colour scheme cannot be a token set.

## Acceptance
- Given the component sources, when they are searched for raw hex, rgb() or named colours, then there are none; every colour is a `--color-*` token.
- Given any page, when it is rendered before and after the change, then it looks the same, pixel for pixel.
- Given the change, when the tokens file is diffed, then no new colour value is added and no existing value is changed.
- Given a component, when it is reviewed, then it does not contain a colour that is not a token.

## Boundaries
- Must not change any colour a user sees.
- Must not add new colour values to the palette.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bringing code in line with a rule in `specs/` when nothing visible changes).

key: SCHED-4418
title: "week view: first day of the week follows the account locale"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-1966]
---

## Intent
Week view always starts on Sunday. Start it on the first day of the week that the account's locale gives (an Account has a locale, specs/product.md).

## Acceptance
- Given an account with locale de-DE, when week view opens, then the week starts on Monday.
- Given an account with locale en-US, when week view opens, then the week starts on Sunday, as now.
- Given any locale, when the week start changes, then no booking moves to another day and no stored time changes (PRD-2): bookings are not moved, only the column order is.

Request IN-1966 (desk): a studio in Berlin says the calendar starts the week on Sunday; their staff expect Monday.

## Boundaries
- Must not change stored bookings or times.
- Must not add a per-user setting; the account locale decides.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes and small features inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

key: SCHED-4446
title: "CSV export: times carry no UTC offset"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:analytics]
---

## Intent
Start and end times in the CSV export have no offset, so every tool that reads them has to guess the zone. Add a UTC offset column next to them, as ADR-0001 asks of data that leaves the product.

## Acceptance
- Given an export for an account in Europe/Berlin in summer, when it is generated, then each row has a UTC offset column with +02:00 next to start and end.
- Given an existing export, when it is generated after the change, then every column it had is still there, with the same name, order and value format (PRD-3).
- Given a row, when its offset is read, then it is not blank.

## Boundaries
- Must not change, rename, reorder or reformat the existing start and end columns.
- Must not remove any column.

Allowed by AUT-1 (new columns, filters or fields that add to what is there and take nothing away).

key: SCHED-4452
title: "calendar sync: Outlook events arrive twice"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
---

## Intent
Some Outlook calendars show each booking twice after a sync. ADR-0002 says each booking is pushed once, with a stable id, so the calendar can tell an update from a new event. Make the Outlook push follow that.

## Acceptance
- Given a booking pushed to an Outlook calendar, when the sync runs again, then the calendar still shows it once.
- Given a booking that changes in sched-prod, when it is pushed again, then Outlook updates the same event, by the same id, and does not add a second one.
- Given a test, when it runs, then it shows a second sync does not create a duplicate.

## Boundaries
- Must not read events back from external calendars (ADR-0002: sync is one-way).
- Must not change the id of bookings already pushed.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes and small features inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

title: "API: rate-limit replies carry no Retry-After header"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:client]
---

## Intent
When the API rate-limits a caller, the 429 reply does not say when to try again. Add a Retry-After header with the seconds until the limit resets.

- Given the 429 reply, when it is read, then its status and body are the same as before.

## Boundaries
- Must not change the rate limits themselves.
- Must not change any reply body.

Allowed by AUT-1 (new columns, filters or fields that add to what is there and take nothing away).

key: SCHED-4486
title: "audit log: keep 90 days"
status: open
labels: [needs-human, from:finance]
---

## Question
Audit log entries are kept now. Finance asks to delete them after 90 days. Should stored audit entries be deleted, and from when?

## Options
1. Delete entries older than 90 days, including the ones already stored.
2. Delete after 90 days only for entries written from now on; keep what is stored.
3. Move entries older than 90 days to an archive instead of deleting them.

## Recommendation
Option 3, unless finance confirms no law or client contract needs the entries for longer.

## Why
Because deleting data that is already stored needs a person (AUT-2), and a deleted audit entry cannot be brought back.

## Acceptance

- Given that booking, when it is opened from either day, then it is the same one booking (PRD-1), not two.
- Given a booking inside one day, when week view shows it, then it does not appear on any other day.

## Boundaries
- Must not split the stored booking or change its times.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes and small features inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

title: "confirmation email: the cancel link opens the login page"

## Intent
The cancel link in the booking confirmation email asks for a login, but people who booked have no account. Make it open the booking without a login, as the cancel link in the reminder email already does.

## Acceptance
- Given a booking confirmation email, when its cancel link is opened by someone without an account, then the booking opens with its cancel action, with no login page.
- Given the reminder email, when its cancel link is opened, then it works as now.
- Given a cancel link for one booking, when it is opened, then it does not show or cancel any other booking.

## Boundaries
- Must not change the reminder email or the sender address.
- Must not open other account pages without a login.

Request IN-5481 (mail): "People who booked with us can't cancel: the link in their confirmation email sends them to a login page."

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes and small features inside the specs, with a test that shows the change).

skill.name: triage
skill.text:
---
name: triage
description: Use when requests (support tickets, chat, client mail, backlog items) must go into an issue tracker so that every open issue is either ready for an agent (agent-ready) or marked for a person (needs-human). Requests in, a marked tracker out.
---

# triage

Input: a tracker of Markdown issue files (one file per issue, YAML-ish frontmatter) and the product's
rules (`specs/`). Output: the same tracker where

- every request id (`IN-…`) is in the `sources` of exactly one issue,
- every issue is `open`, `done` (work that shipped) or `closed` with a `reason`
  (`duplicate` · `obsolete` · `contradicts-spec` · `not-planned`),
- every open issue carries exactly one mark: `agent-ready` or `needs-human`,
- every body cites the rule, issue key or request id that decided it.

The tracker's own README defines the format. Read it first; where it differs from this skill, the
README wins.

## Steps

1. **Collect.** Run the tracker's collector. Run it again before you hand in: channels keep
   receiving requests, and a request you never saw is an unmarked issue.
2. **Read the rules whole.** Every file in `specs/`, including decisions. List each rule id with one
   line on what it allows or forbids. The autonomy rules (who may do what alone) decide the mark;
   the product and design rules decide whether a request is allowed at all.
3. **Read every issue and request whole.** Ignore urgency, rank and who is shouting: "URGENT", "this
   week", "one-line change" change nothing about the mark. Note for each:
   - Is it already done? (A backlog item marked done, or a request that describes a bug a done item
     fixed, and was filed before that fix.) → `closed`, `duplicate`, `duplicate-of` the done issue.
   - Does it ask for something a spec forbids? → `closed`, `contradicts-spec`, cite the rule id.
   - Does it ask for no work (a "please don't change X")? → `closed`, `not-planned`, and keep it as
     a constraint: any later issue that would touch X is `needs-human`, citing this request id.
   - Does it duplicate another open issue? → merge: one issue, both ids in `sources`.
   - Does one ticket hold two problems ("merged by …", "and the … too")? → split: one issue per
     problem, each with the ticket id in `sources`, each body naming the other.
   - Does a new request clash with an earlier one (one asks for a change, another says "we rely on
     it, don't change it")? → one `needs-human` issue with both ids in `sources`; close nothing.
   - Does a request withdraw an earlier one ("scratch my request …")? → close the earlier issue
     `not-planned`, both ids in `sources`, the withdrawal cited.
4. **Mark each open issue.** Walk the autonomy rules in order:
   - `needs-human` if it touches anything on the "needs a human" list: something a client said they
     rely on, pricing / invoices / terms, deleting or rewriting stored data. Also when the request
     changes existing behaviour other clients get (an existing export format, a schedule everyone
     gets) and the specs do not settle it: a person picks between options.
   - `agent-ready` only if a line on the "may do alone" list covers it. Name that line.
   - Neither fits → `needs-human`.
5. **Find blockers.** An issue that needs another to ship first (a theme needs colours in tokens,
   a denser layout needs spacing on the scale, a text-size setting needs the type scale) gets
   `blocked-by: [KEY]`. Read the backlog bodies for "until this ships, … cannot …".
6. **Write the bodies** in the README's shapes:
   - agent-ready: `## Intent`, `## Acceptance` (Given/When/Then lines, at least one "… not …"
     case), `## Boundaries` (must not touch …), and a closing line `Allowed by AUT-n (<the line>).`
   - needs-human: `## Question`, `## Options` (two or more, numbered), `## Recommendation`
     (`Option n`), `## Why` (`Because … (<id>)`).
   - closed: one or two sentences on what decided it, with the id.
   Keep the `from:` labels. Keep backlog keys. A request issue keeps its `IN-…` key.
7. **Check.** Run `node <this skill>/scripts/check.mjs <tracker dir> [--api URL --session TOKEN]`.
   With the API it also proves every request id from every channel is in some `sources`. Fix every
   line it prints, then run it again until it prints `ok`.

## Rules of thumb

- A mark is a decision about who acts, not about how hard the work is. A one-line change to an
  export a client's tools read is still a person's call.
- Done means shipped. Do not reopen a done issue because nobody signed it; do close requests
  that it answers as duplicates of it.
- Never pick a side between two people's requests yourself: that is a `needs-human` question,
  with both request ids in `sources`.
- Cite by id (`AUT-1`, `DES-5`, `PRD-3`, `ADR-0002`, `SCHED-4446`, `IN-8530`), never "the spec".
